title: I'm building an open-world game of the real Earth with AI coding agents - here's where it is
author: RasacL
selftext:
Every street comes from OpenStreetMap and the terrain from open elevation data, so you can drive or walk anywhere. This clip is Niagara, Paris, Bengaluru, Dubai, Tokyo and Istanbul, recorded from the current build. It runs in the browser (three.js, WebGPU).

![video](y2l8bf1eel1i1 "HyperHoods Open-world game")

  
How it's made: 2 weeks in, almost all the code is written by AI agents Claude Code. I decide what gets built and test it; for bigger changes one agent builds and a separate agent reviews before anything merges. One rule I keep: no hand-fixing places. If Paris looks wrong, the fix has to be a rule that works everywhere, which is what lets one person cover the whole planet.

The thing I'd love input on: **buildings.** Everything is generated from OpenStreetMap footprints, heights and tags, with no hand-made models, because it has to work for every city on Earth. Right now that means window layouts, shop fronts at street level and regional wall colours, but streets still look samey up close. If you've made procedural buildings look good at scale, what worked? Shader-based facades, AI-generated texture sets per region, kitbashed modules, something else?

What still breaks: big interchanges, some landmarks are simple stand-ins, and phones are slower.

Side note: I haven't posted the link anywhere until today, but it already gets **\~400 visitors a day,** mostly from Google and ChatGPT recommending it, with average sessions around 6 minutes. Still figuring out why ChatGPT picked it up.

Link in the comments. Happy to answer anything about the workflow.
